Emote
ee-MOHT
noun / verb (Gen Alpha slang)
A back-formation from emotion; as a verb ("to emote," to show emotion theatrically) it dates to early-twentieth-century American theater slang. Online, early text games (MUDs, 1990s) gave players an "emote" command for describing actions, and later online games turned emotes into animated gestures. Fortnite (2017) made emotes into dances — the Floss, the Default Dance, the Griddy — several copied from celebrities and viral videos, prompting lawsuits in 2018–19 that were dropped or dismissed. Gen Alpha uses "emote" for the dances themselves and "emoting on" someone for dancing over a defeated opponent.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In Gen Alpha usage an emote is a game dance or gesture, and children do them in real life at recess. "Emoting on" someone means dancing over a player you just beat — a taunt. The Christian observation: dancing and gesture are part of God’s good world. "To every thing there is a season... a time to mourn, and a time to dance" (Ecc 3:1, 4), and David "danced before the LORD with all his might" (2Sa 6:14). Joy that bursts out of the body is not a sin. But the taunting emote turns joy into mockery, and Scripture names that, too: "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise" (Mic 7:8). The test of an emote is the test of the heart — is it gladness, or gloating? Paul’s rule for the whole body applies to dances: "Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep" (Rom 12:15). A father can tell a five-year-old: "It’s fun to do a happy dance! But we don’t dance to make someone feel bad when they lose. We dance because we’re glad — and the best reason to be glad is God."

Webster 1828 Definition

Game gesture or dance (MUD command, 1990s; Fortnite dances, 2017-) — the body’s joy, good in its season, sinful when it becomes a taunt over the fallen.

EMOTE, n. / v. (theater slang, early 20th c.; game usage 1990s–present; Gen Alpha usage) An animated dance or gesture performed by a game character; to perform one. "I have the Floss emote."

Emote on (someone) — to dance over a defeated player as a taunt.

Older sense: to display emotion theatrically ("the actor emoted wildly").

Decode for parents: harmless as dance; watch for the taunt.

Key Scripture

Ecc 3:4 — "A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;"

2Sa 6:14 — "And David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod."

Mic 7:8 — "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me."

Rom 12:15 — "Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep."

Modern Corruption

The emote is the body’s joy put on a button; it is good in its season and turns sour when it becomes a dance over a defeated neighbor.

expand to see more

There is nothing wrong with a happy dance, and much right with it. The corruption is the culture of the taunt — emoting on the fallen, celebrating another’s defeat with the body. Games reward it because it feels powerful, and children carry it onto the field. Proverbs warns against gladness at a stumble; Micah gives the fallen man’s reply.

Keep the dances and train the heart. Make the family rule that we celebrate our win and help the loser up. Teach the child that David’s dance was before the LORD, not over Michal. The best emote is gratitude moving the feet.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Emotion → back-formation emote (early 20th-c. theater slang) → MUD emote command (1990s) → Fortnite dance emotes (2017).

Latin emovere, to move out, stir up → emotion

Early 20th-c. American theater: to emote, to act out feeling

1990s text games: the emote command

2017-: Fortnite dance emotes; 2018–19 lawsuits over copied dances

Gen Alpha: emote on, to taunt by dancing

Usage

""He eliminated me and then emoted on me. Rude.""

"A time to dance — not over the fallen (Ecc 3:4; Mic 7:8)."

"David danced before the LORD; that is the best emote (2Sa 6:14)."
